forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329120647_c4ea7dea
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(x_s) = s for each s in I. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Assume M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Then there exists a family (f_s)_{s in I} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing order of s is a regular sequence in R. If I is empty, this means the empty family.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: Let a and b be integers with 0 <= a <= b, and let S := Q[y_1,...,y_b] be graded by deg(y_i)=i. Suppose g_1,...,g_a are homogeneous elements of S that form a regular sequence and satisfy deg(g_i)=i for each i=1,...,a. Then there exists a graded Q-algebra automorphism phi : S -> S such that phi(g_i)=y_i for every i=1,...,a. When a=0, phi may be taken to be the identity automorphism.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Proof. We construct, by induction on m=0,1,...,a, a graded Q-algebra automorphism phi_m of S such that phi_m(g_i)=y_i for every i with 1<=i<=m.

For m=0, let phi_0 be the identity on S. This already gives the stated special case a=0.

Now fix m with 1<=m<=a and assume phi_{m-1} has been constructed. Put h:=phi_{m-1}(g_m). Because phi_{m-1} is graded and deg(g_m)=m, the element h is homogeneous of weighted degree m.

Since phi_{m-1} is an automorphism, it induces an isomorphism of quotient rings
S/(g_1,...,g_{m-1}) -> S/(phi_{m-1}(g_1),...,phi_{m-1}(g_{m-1})) = S/(y_1,...,y_{m-1}),
sending the class of g_m to the class of h. Because g_1,...,g_a is a regular sequence, the class of g_m is a nonzerodivisor in S/(g_1,...,g_{m-1}); therefore the class of h is a nonzerodivisor in S/(y_1,...,y_{m-1}).

We now determine the shape of h. Consider any monomial y_1^{e_1}...y_b^{e_b} occurring in h. Its weighted degree is sum_{j=1}^b j e_j = m. Hence e_j=0 for all j>m, because j>m would already contribute more than m. Also, if e_m>0, then m e_m<=m, so e_m=1; and then all e_j with j<m must be 0, since every degree is positive. Therefore any monomial of h that involves y_m is exactly y_m itself. It follows that
h = c y_m + p
for some c in Q and some homogeneous polynomial p in Q[y_1,...,y_{m-1}] of degree m. (For m=1 this simply means p=0.)

Passing to the quotient S/(y_1,...,y_{m-1}), the class of h becomes c y_m. But S/(y_1,...,y_{m-1}) is isomorphic to Q[y_m,...,y_b], so it is a nonzero ring. Since the class of h is a nonzerodivisor there, it is in particular nonzero. Thus c y_m is nonzero in Q[y_m,...,y_b], which forces c!=0.

Define tau_m on the generators of S by
- tau_m(y_j)=y_j for j!=m,
- tau_m(y_m)=c^{-1}(y_m-p).
By the universal property of the polynomial ring, this defines a Q-algebra endomorphism of S. Because p involves only y_1,...,y_{m-1}, which tau_m fixes, the inverse map is given on generators by
- tau_m^{-1}(y_j)=y_j for j!=m,
- tau_m^{-1}(y_m)=c y_m + p.
Hence tau_m is a Q-algebra automorphism. It is graded, because tau_m(y_j) is homogeneous of degree j for every j: this is obvious for j!=m, and for j=m both y_m and p have degree m.

Now tau_m fixes y_1,...,y_{m-1}, so for i<m we have
phi_m(g_i)=tau_m(phi_{m-1}(g_i))=tau_m(y_i)=y_i,
where phi_m:=tau_m composed with phi_{m-1}. Also,
phi_m(g_m)=tau_m(h)=tau_m(c y_m+p)=c c^{-1}(y_m-p)+p=y_m.
Thus phi_m is a graded Q-algebra automorphism satisfying phi_m(g_i)=y_i for all 1<=i<=m.

This completes the induction step. Therefore phi_a exists and is a graded Q-algebra automorphism of S with phi_a(g_i)=y_i for every i=1,...,a. When a=0, the identity automorphism works. This proves the lemma.
result_payload.proof_summary: Inductively normalize the sequence. After sending g_1,...,g_{m-1} to y_1,...,y_{m-1}, the image of g_m is a homogeneous degree-m polynomial h. Weighted-degree considerations force h=c y_m+p(y_1,...,y_{m-1}); regularity implies its class mod (y_1,...,y_{m-1}) is a nonzerodivisor, hence nonzero, so c!=0. A triangular graded automorphism fixing earlier variables and sending c y_m+p to y_m completes the induction.
